newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end sharply lower on finance sales.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end sharply lower on finance sales.

text.p: Thai share prices fell sharply at the close on Thursday as renewed rumours about the health of local finance companies prompted investors to offload finance shares, brokers said.

"The finance sector led the market fall today. When the economy remains sluggish, there will always be rumours about the financial health of finance companies," one broker at MCC Finance and Securities.
The SET index closed down 13.81 points or 1.87 percent at 726.01 on 5.99 billion baht trade. The SET-50 fell 1.35 points to 53.43.
Brokers said that key central economic data released late on Thursday had no impact on the market as most of the figures were the same as those isued by the finance ministry on Wednesday.
Worries about higher U.S. interest rates following US Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's remarks to legislators also affected the market today, analysts said.

"If interest rates rise in the U.S., interest rates will also rise in Thailand," said Robert Burgess, head of equity research at First Bangkok City Finance and Securities. "The stock market will decline more as higher interest rates will raise (listed) corporations' interest rate expenses."
The hike in interest rates could also slow further economic growth, he said.
Finance and banking sectors tumbled 5.07 percent and 2.39 percent respectively.
Finance One plunged 2.50 baht to 25.50 on most active trade of 395 million baht.
National Finance slipped three to 34 and General Finance lost 2.25 to 27.50.
Thai Farmers Bank lost five to 110, Krung Thai Bank was down one to 39.50.
